Sophia L: Heads-up — saw ~2x p99 latency yesterday during the 14:00 UTC window for qwen2.5 host pool. Profiling points to a kernel selector flip to a generic path after a KV cache invalidation triggered by tokenizer splits on CJK input. Anyone seen this pattern before?

Ryan P: Can you drop the profiler snippet + example input?

Sophia L: Pasted repro and minimal logs below. Repro input is a ~3k char Chinese doc which causes multiple token splits across sentences.

Maria G: profiler output (trimmed):
```
attn_kernel_selector: autokernel -> fallback_generic
kv_cache_invalidate: true (prefix mismatch)
batcher: window=16 -> raised to 64 requeue
latency_p99: 420ms -> 860ms (after flip)
GPU_util: 63% -> 91%
```

Anya K: interesting — tokenizer split count spikes cause lots of tiny KV keys being created and invalidated, which can nudge the kernel heuristic toward non-optimized codepath. Also ALiBi vs RoPE variants show different kv layout in our runtime (we saw head/kv dim offsets).

Kevin T: repro command I used: `python -m runtime.profile --model qwen2.5 --input tests/fixtures/cjk_long.txt --batch 8 --trace-kv`

Sophia L: @Kevin T thanks. Confirmed that toggling `--attn-variant=rope` vs `--attn-variant=alibi` changes whether autokernel picks fused attention kernels. With ALiBi we hit fallback more often.

perf-bot: deploy/infra-note: observed increased fallbacks 2024-11-08T14:03Z across pool redwood-qwen2p5-eu-1, spike lasted ~12m.

Sachin R: Two quick hypotheses: 1) our kernel-selection threshold heuristics are overly sensitive to per-token head/kv dimensionality misreports coming from the tokenizer splitter. 2) batcher expanding to 64 increases memory pressure, forcing fallback scheduling.

Maria G: I ran a tight bisect; changing `kernel_selector.threshold_autokernel` from 0.12 -> 0.08 reduces fallback frequency for these inputs and restores p99 to ~450ms. But that's a heuristic tweak. Long-term we should handle tokenizer-side kv key consistency.

Anya K: On the tokenizer side, multilang splitter currently emits soft-splits for CJK which we treat as new token boundaries; we could instead coalesce adjacent splits into a single KV chunk for runtime to avoid churn. Patch idea: coalesce if consecutive splits < 6 bytes.

Ryan P: Is there a testcase we can add to runtime unit tests to prevent regression?

Kevin T: Added local test `tests/eng_runtime/regressions/qwen2p5/cjk_kv_churn.py` that simulates repeated split/merge and asserts autokernel stays chosen. I'll PR after validation.

Sophia L: Action items: 1) Kevin to PR kernel_selector threshold change + unit test (short term), 2) Anya to prototype tokenizer coalescing patch (medium term), 3) Maria to run a 24h canary on eu pool with synthetic CJK traces (verify p50/p95/p99). I'll create canary job.

Maria G: Canary job created -> `canary/qwen2p5-cjk-kv-churn-v1`, running now. Will report metrics in #eng-runtime when complete.

Sophia L: Thanks all — marking as triage/assign. If anyone sees related alerts, ping me. :thumbsup:

Kevin T: quick note — when testing, also try `--kv-heads=16` vs default 8; some Qwen forks expose different kv heads which changes memory layout and can hide/fix the flip.

Anya K: ack, I'll include kv-head permutations in the tokenizer prototype runs.

perf-bot: note: scheduled perf-regression-check for qwen2p5 pool in 2h.
